This is a great example illustrating the fact that sometimes statistically significant doesn't equate with clinical significance. Say for example I have 2 medicines for blood pressure. Suppose that the truth in the universe is that X decreases systolic BP to an average of 122, while Y decreases it to an average of 125. If you do a big enough study you will find a statistically significant difference between the two drugs. However that doesn't translate to a clinically significant difference in that someone with an average systolic BP of 122 is no different with regard to risks of untreated hypertension like stroke and heart disease than 125 is. So using either drug X or Y will still give you the same benefit in preventing these problems.
